key_insight: The paper shows that an LLM can help generate a formal, human-readable proof of the irrationality of √2, with LPTP providing the final proof check.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a practical workflow for combining language models with theorem provers to accelerate formal verification in logic programming and mathematical software.
method: Start from basic pure logic program predicate definitions.
Use LPTP natural-deduction proofs to formalize the classic irrationality argument.
Iteratively interact with an LLM, then verify the resulting proof fully in LPTP.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a single case study: a complete formal proof was partially generated by an LLM and fully proof-checked by LPTP.
watch_item: The result is a proof-of-concept on one classic theorem, so broader reliability and scalability for harder proofs remain untested.
paper_title: Case study: proving sqrt(2) irrational with LPTP and an LLM
